correctness.rationale: PASS: In the stated four-orientation quarter-turn harmonic model, the published stationary rotated coordinates U,V are independent with density (1-z²)^{β-1}/B(1/2,β) on (-1,1). Then S=ρ²=U²+V² is the sum of independent Beta(1/2,β) variables; p(ρ)=2ρ g(ρ²), so the radial Jacobian is correct. Direct beta convolution for 1<s<2 with t=2-s gives p(sqrt(2-t))=4 B(β,β)t^{2β-1} Hβ(t/(2-t))/[B(1/2,β)^2 sqrt(2-t)], Hβ(w)=2F1(1/2,1/2;β+1/2;w²). Its positive-power-series tilted mean Q=wH'/H has dQ/dlog w=Var(2n)>0. Thus eta=t dlog p/dt=2β-1+t/[2(2-t)]+2Q/(2-t) strictly increases; it starts negative iff β<1/2 and diverges at t->1 for β<1/2, giving one outer valley and two integrable shell peaks. For β>=1/2 eta>0, hence monotone radial decrease for 1<ρ<sqrt2; for β<=1 inner radial density is strictly increasing. Independent scipy evaluations at β=.25,.4,.49,.5,.75,1.3 confirm monotone eta and β=.25 valley t=0.6353250926701738; they are corroboration of the analytic argument. At β=.5 logarithmic singularity at ρ=1 and outer limit 2sqrt2/pi; near threshold tβ=4(1-2β)+O((1-2β)^2). Precise β>1 inner mode classification is not claimed.
